questions.stem: A company wants to turn on a new checkout feature in production without redeploying application code. The change must reach users gradually. If a CloudWatch alarm on checkout errors goes off while the change is rolling out, or during a monitoring period after it reaches all targets, the change must be reverted automatically. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Store the flag as an AWS Lambda environment variable, and use a CodeDeploy canary deployment to publish a new function version.
Store the flag in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and have an operator change it back if the alarm goes off.
Use an AWS AppConfig feature flag with a gradual deployment strategy that has a bake time, and attach the CloudWatch alarm as a rollback monitor.
Build a new container image with the flag enabled, and roll it out with an ECS rolling update.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer configures AWS AppConfig deployments with CloudWatch alarms as rollback monitors. The team wants to understand exactly when a rollback happens and what it needs, so that it can rely on the feature instead of watching each deployment. Which statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: If a monitored alarm goes into the ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA state during a deployment, AWS AppConfig rolls back the configuration data to the previous version.
AWS AppConfig needs permissions to be configured before it can roll back deployments based on CloudWatch alarms.
AWS AppConfig rolls back only after an operator approves the rollback in the console.
A rollback redeploys the previous version of the application code to the compute targets.
AWS AppConfig stops monitoring alarms as soon as the configuration reaches 100% of its targets.

questions.stem: When the Systems Manager parameter /app/db-endpoint is updated, the company must restart the application on a fleet of instances so that they read the new value. A senior engineer must approve each restart before it happens, and the company does not want to write or host custom code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event, with a Systems Manager Automation runbook as the target that includes an aws:approve step before the restart.
Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event that invokes an AWS Lambda function, which emails the engineer and waits for a reply before restarting.
Create an EventBridge rule for the parameter update event, with a Systems Manager Automation runbook as the target that restarts the application immediately.
Have the engineer check the parameter history every morning and restart the application by hand when the value has changed.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer must run a Systems Manager Automation runbook that changes a configuration file on 400 managed instances. No more than 20 instances may run the change at the same time. The company allows up to 5 instances to fail; after that, Systems Manager must stop sending the change to the remaining instances. Which approach meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Run the automation with rate control, set the concurrency to 20, and set the error threshold to 5.
Run the automation with adaptive concurrency so that Systems Manager raises the number of concurrent runs automatically.
Write a script that starts the runbook on 20 instances, waits, counts failures, and repeats until all instances are done.
Run the automation one instance at a time from the console, and stop when 5 instances have failed.
